analysis.investment_thesis: Paras Defence is a legitimate niche defense/space business benefiting from India's Atmanirbhar Bharat push, but the Magic Formula screams overvaluation — Earnings Yield of ~1.5% (EBIT INR 100 Cr / EV ~INR 6,511 Cr) is 10x below my minimum threshold. The business earns a mediocre ROCE of ~15.6%, nowhere near the quality premium this price demands.
key_strengths: FY2025 earnings acceleration: revenue +44% to INR 365 Cr, EBITDA doubled to INR 101 Cr — strong execution
Near-zero leverage (D/E 0.08, net debt negative at ~INR -10 Cr) gives balance sheet optionality
Niche moat in optics, EMP shielding, space structures — hard-to-replicate defense-grade capabilities
key_risks: Valuation is extreme: P/E 88.8x, EV/EBITDA 61.3x — priced for perfection with zero margin of safety
FCF is deeply erratic: -INR 71 Cr in FY2024, only +INR 10 Cr in FY2025 despite INR 61 Cr net profit — working capital and capex intensity destroy conversion
Revenue base is tiny (INR 365 Cr) with lumpy government defense orders; any order delay compresses earnings dramatically
red_flags: Earnings Yield of ~1.54% — 65 years of current EBIT to recover enterprise value
ROCE of 15.6% and ROE of 11.5% — well below the 20-25% threshold needed to justify this premium
FY2024 OCF was -INR 46 Cr on INR 30 Cr net profit — earnings quality concern; profits don't reliably convert to cash
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on Paras Defence produces a near-failing grade on both axes. Earnings Yield (EBIT/EV) = INR 100 Cr / ~INR 6,511 Cr = 1.54% — catastrophically below my 12% attractiveness floor. Return on Capital (proxied by stated ROCE) is 15.6%, which is decent for a government-dependent manufacturer but falls short of the 20%+ I require before paying any meaningful premium. The business is not bad — it has real products, real differentiation in optics and EMP shielding, and a structural tailwind from India's defense indigenization. But the market has already priced in a decade of high-growth optimism. The FY2025 EBITDA doubling (INR 54 Cr → INR 101 Cr) looks impressive until you note FCF was only INR 10 Cr on INR 35 Cr of capex and continued working capital drag.

The Magic Formula is a ranking exercise — you buy the cheapest good businesses, not the most exciting ones. At EV/EBITDA of 61x, Paras sits in the bottom decile of earnings yield globally, let alone in India. Even if the company grows EBIT at 20% annually for five years (reaching ~INR 250 Cr), the earnings yield barely crosses 3.8% at today's price — still unattractive. I require a margin of safety; this stock offers the opposite. Pass.
